title: Copy selected objects and rotate the copy at its new position
statement: A copy-rotate is composed from native CAD commands: the selection is copied in place (base 0,0 displaced by @), the copy (the previous selection set) is then moved by a user-picked base and second point, and finally rotated about the system LASTPOINT (the move's second point) by a user-entered angle. The routine creates nothing programmatically; the documented outcome of the rule is a fixed command sequence whose result is a displaced, rotated duplicate of the selection. No disposition on a target platform is inferred from the existence of native commands there.
inputs: base point and second point for the move

evidence.detail: Copy-in-place line 20; move of previous selection with pause line 27; rotation base read from LASTPOINT lines 30-32.

authority.basis: generic drafting convenience macro; no firm-specific content

uncertainty: Two princ strings begin with a backslash before P and S (unrecognized AutoLISP escape sequences); if the file loads in AutoCAD as its author used it, the strings apparently load — behavior unverified, needs a recorded run
(while (= sel nil) ...) uses numeric equality on nil — works for the empty-selection case in AutoLISP but is fragile style
'ent' is setq'd at line 10 but never used and is not declared local — a stray global
The sequence relies on _P (previous selection) surviving across three command calls; AutoCAD maintains it, IntelliCAD/BricsCAD behavior unverified although the readme claims cross-CAD support
No run of c:cr exists in LLCO evidence; the composed command sequence is a static reading only

legacy_defect.description: Suspected defects (existence of the code patterns is observed; runtime impact unverified): suspected invalid escape sequences in two princ strings (may fail or print unexpectedly on load); stray global 'ent'; nil compared with numeric =. None affect geometry if the strings load.

required_human_ruling: Disposition of this rule on any target platform (keep_for_compatibility / fix / retire) is reserved to the estate's acceptance authority. LLCO records the rule's documented outcome — a fixed copy-move-rotate command sequence — and does not infer disposition from the existence of comparable native commands on a candidate target platform.
